porcelain-prisoner-1709.d:
Augustus the Strong of Saxony held the young alchemist Johann Friedrich Böttger prisoner, demanding gold. Böttger never made gold, but working with Ehrenfried Walther von Tschirnhaus he cracked the secret of hard-paste porcelain. In 1710 the Meissen factory was founded.

rooster-pearl-300ad.d:

aqua-regia-nobel.t: He DISSOLVED two Nobel medals to hide them from the Nazis #shorts
aqua-regia-nobel.d:
Aqua regia, 'royal water', a mix of nitric and hydrochloric acid known to medieval alchemists, dissolves gold. In 1940 chemist George de Hevesy dissolved the Nobel medals of Max von Laue and James Franck in Copenhagen so the Nazis could not find them. After the war the gold was recovered and the Nobel Foundation recast the medals.

prussian-blue-1706.t: He wanted RED. A dirty jar gave the world a new blue #shorts
prussian-blue-1706.d:
Around 1706 in Berlin, color maker Johann Jacob Diesbach tried to make a red pigment, using potash from the alchemist Johann Konrad Dippel that had been tainted with Dippel's animal oil. He got a deep blue instead: Prussian blue, the first modern synthetic pigment. It colors Hokusai's Great Wave, and today it is also a medicine against certain radioactive poisoning.

gunpowder-elixir.d:
Chinese Taoist alchemists searched for an elixir of immortality. A text from around 850 AD warns that heating sulfur, realgar and saltpeter with honey made flames that burned hands, faces and whole houses. By 1044 the military manual Wujing Zongyao printed the first known gunpowder formulas.

aqua-vitae-whisky.t: Whisky started as MEDICINE called 'water of life' #shorts
aqua-vitae-whisky.d:
Medieval European alchemists and physicians distilled wine into 'aqua vitae', the water of life, and sold it as medicine. The Gaelic name, uisge beatha, became 'whisky'. The first written record of Scotch is a 1494 royal account: malt for Friar John Cor 'to make aqua vitae'.
